section: Sections/04b-representation.tex, sec:res-used, steps one to three

_v10_no_value_changed.statement: NOT ONE PLOTTED OR PRINTED VALUE CHANGED IN v10. The seven gate fractions are the same seven floats, unrounded; 0.8, 0.41--0.82, 0.121, 0.083, 0.90--0.95, 0.620, 0.031, 480, twelve, forty, ten, eleven and seven are all unmoved and every one is listed below with its key path.
_v10_no_value_changed.what_did_change: the two value-to-position maps, and therefore every drawn coordinate. Both the old and the new map are recorded under value_to_position_maps so the audit can redo either. A map change is a position change, not a value change.
superseded_claims: v9's verification.repair_pass_9 said 'NO NUMBER CHANGED' of pass 9 and that remains true of pass 9; v10 makes the same claim of itself, on the same terms.

v9's text_agreement_checks entry for figs/slab.json asserted that purify's 0.031 and slab's 0.031 are the 'same source field, same rounding, so the two figures cannot drift'. THAT IS FALSE and is corrected in place below: purify prints layer 9 and slab prints the seven-layer MEAN. See _corrected_v9_error_the_two_0031s.

_corrected_v9_error_the_two_0031s.v9_claim: figs/slab.json purified_drug_slab_Vpure.per_layer.9 -- '0.030620247335072275, printed 0.031' -- 'same source field, same rounding, so the two figures cannot drift'. Result recorded OK.
_corrected_v9_error_the_two_0031s.why_it_is_false: The two figures print the same three digits for two DIFFERENT quantities. fig:purify prints workspace_probe.json :: layers.9.variance_share.drug_pure = 0.030620247335072275, a single layer, and says 'at layer 9' on the drawing so a reader cannot take it for a summary. figs/slab.tex prints figs/slab.json :: purified_drug_slab_Vpure.mean = 0.03145888409003616, the mean over all seven layers, and draws its 11.3252-degree wedge to that mean. The two agree only because both round to 0.031 at three places. They WILL drift the moment either is reported to four places: 0.0306 against 0.0315.
_corrected_v9_error_the_two_0031s.action_taken: the assertion is retracted here. The layer-9 qualifier on purify's drawing is load-bearing and must survive any future edit; it is the only thing on the page that keeps the two numbers apart. No number changed and neither figure is wrong; the LEDGER was wrong.

previous_v9.why_it_moved: the spine moved right to open a lane for the rotated axis label, and the fraction span grew so that the axis midpoint sits exactly at the centre of that lane. See the v10 header, item 4.

current_v11.why_the_origin_rose: 1.45 -> 1.75 buys 2.8mm of white between the layer numerals and the word 'layer'. At v10's 0.63mm the word sat directly under the numeral 2, one type size larger than it, and the pair read as 'layer 2' -- the same fault the pass-9 note in purify.tex records against the old placement under the layer-9 numeral, reintroduced at layer 2. The repair is vertical so that the contract's left-alignment of the x-axis label survives.
current_v11.why_the_span_fell: 3.85 -> 3.00 takes 0.68cm out of the empty fail region, which at v10's span was 21.6% of the content box and the largest object on the page, and gives it to the gap between the schematic band and panel (c). The full 0-to-1 RANGE is untouched: decision 12 in purify.tex stands. The region keeps its exact 80% share of the axis and falls to 16.8% of the content box.

previous_v10.header_disagreement_corrected_in_v11: purify.tex's v10 header stated the change as 'the y map (0.75 + f*2.10 -> 1.45 + f*3.95) and the x map (1.05 + (L-2)/14*11.00 -> 1.45 + (L-2)/14*11.75)'. Four of those coefficients are wrong: v10 shipped f*3.85 and 1.85 + (L-2)/14*12.00, which is what this ledger recorded and what the render measures. An auditor working from the header would have put layer 16 at 13.20cm against the 13.85cm drawn and the gate at 4.61cm against 4.53cm. The header is superseded in place, per S25; no mark ever moved because of it.

_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.verdict: The slab that is projected out. NOT V_pure, and the figure, its caption and this ledger nowhere claim V_pure.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.why: workspace_probe.json stores exactly ONE ablated accuracy series, layers.<L>.drug_decode_ablated, and frac_signal_removed reproduces from the RAW decode by exact float equality at all seven layers (see identity_check below). The section-4.5 arm files prove the pipeline can distinguish the two cases: they store drug_decode_ablated AND drug_decode_pure_ablated, frac_signal_removed AND frac_signal_removed_pure. This file stores only the first of each pair.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.figure_wording_v9: panel three's subtitle said 'projecting the drug subspace out', the section's own noun at 04b-representation.tex:184-185, and the string V_pure did not appear in panel three.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.figure_wording_v10: the subtitle is gone with every other subtitle. The axis label says 'fraction of drug signal removed' over '(before minus after)/(before minus chance)', which names the quantity without naming a slab at all, and the caveat 'measured on the slab that is projected out; the stored file has no separate purified-slab gate' moved from the drawing's foot note to the caption to hold text density under 5.0 characters per 100mm^2. The string V_pure still does not appear in panel (c). Nothing about the claim changed; its location did.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.verdict_v11: CORRECTED. The file does not record which subspace was projected out. The drawing, the caption and this ledger therefore say 'the subspace projected out' and attribute the gate to neither the raw slab nor V_pure.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.why_the_v10_reasoning_was_a_non_sequitur: v10 argued the gate is not V_pure's because 'the identity reproduces from the RAW decode'. The identity (drug_decode - drug_decode_ablated)/(drug_decode - chance) == frac_signal_removed fixes only the BEFORE term as the raw probe accuracy; it says nothing whatever about which subspace the ABLATION removed. What can honestly be said is (i) workspace_probe.json stores exactly one ablated series and no purified counterpart, and (ii) the naming convention of the section-4.5 arm files, which store drug_decode_ablated AND drug_decode_pure_ablated, suggests but does not establish that the unsuffixed series is the raw one.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.why_it_matters: where both are stored the purified gate is the LOWER of the two: probe_arm_residual.json :: layers.12 has frac_signal_removed 0.3633540372670808 against frac_signal_removed_pure 0.324087591240876, and drug_decode_ablated 0.611 against drug_decode_pure_ablated 0.6847. So the two cases are not interchangeable and neither may be assumed.
_which_slab_the_gate_is_measured_on.figure_wording_v11: RESTORED TO THE DRAWING. A \scriptsize quietink scope line sits directly under panel (c)'s head at (1.60, 5.00): 'Gate measured on the subspace projected out; no separate gate is stored for $V_{\textrm{pure}}$.' v10 had cut the caveat from the foot note for text density, which left panel (c) with no slab named in its head, axis, ticks, labels or foot, sitting directly under panel (b)'s closing line 'so causal claims use the purified slab, not the raw'. The inference that the gate was run on V_pure was then unavoidable and unsupported.

_intervals.declaration_on_the_drawing: the second of the two \scriptsize quietink foot lines at the figure's own x origin: 'The fraction is (before minus after)/(before minus chance). No interval is returned; the marks are point estimates.' One block, two lines, naming the only panel that carries marks with a scale.
_intervals.why: frac_signal_removed is a single ratio of two accuracies over 480 prompts and carries no stored dispersion of any kind. The KL series in the same file carry [mean, se, n] triples whose se is a normal-approximation SE, not this document's interval convention (95% bootstrap clustered over cell lines); figs/fig-mechanism.json already records intervals_drawn false for that reason. Every mark here is a bare filled disc, which is how this document says a point estimate has no interval.
_intervals.panels_a_and_b: carry no measured mark at all, so there is nothing for an interval to attach to. Their marks are open rulegrey rings, which is this document's glyph for a schematic, unscaled object; that is what says it, and no text says it.

_what_may_not_be_read_off_this_figure: Any accuracy of the twenty-four-class probe sweep of sec:res-mechanism. This panel is scoped to the twelve-class probe, chance 1/12 = 0.0833; the arm files run 24 classes at chance 1/24 and their gate_pass is FALSE at every layer of every arm. fig:mechanism's caption already forbids reading the two accuracy series across, and this figure inherits that.

Any scale for the geometry in panels (a) and (b). The rings, the stems, the cross, the three bands, the confound patch, the removal arrow and the right angle are schematic; only the four printed numbers under panel (b) are measured. From v10 the OPEN RING says this at every mark, against panel (c)'s filled disc, instead of an 8pt footnote apologising for the collision.

Any per-layer ordering of the seven gate fractions. The axis runs 0 to 1 because 0 is the floor of a fraction and because the fail region's height IS the share of the outcome space that would have made every null unfalsifiable; a reviewer asked for the range to be cut to 0.75-1.00 so the seven dots would resolve, and that was overruled, and stays overruled. tab:workspace is the authority for the per-layer values.
A trend across the seven dots. They are drawn as an unconnected set because the series is flat -- 0.8846 to 0.9492 spans 0.249cm on the v10 axis.
A dose reference level. 0.90--0.95 is printed as text and no 0.90 rule is drawn; see dose_cross_decode below.

Any ratio between panel (a)'s band and panel (b)'s bands. They are drawn at the same fill opacity so the glyph rhymes and a reader joins stage one's output to stage two's input; the rhyme is about identity of object, not about size.

fail_region.why_it_changed: Two reasons, both measured. (i) rulegrey!18 over white renders at grey 237 and rulegrey!12 at 243; both are above the 230 threshold the ink budget counts, so neither costs anything, but the lighter fill stops the region reading as the data. A cold reader's eye went to it first: it fills about 80% of the plotting area while the seven dots occupy a band at the top. (ii) The two italic lines inside it restated the caption's own 'the shaded region ... is empty' and sat in the data area competing with the marks. The emptiness is the message and the caption states it.

fail_region.mark_v11: rulegrey!8 filled rectangle, drawn first, no frame, NO TEXT INSIDE IT, and NAMED from outside: 'an untestable null', \scriptsize quietink, anchor=west at (14.25, 2.95), beside the region's own vertical middle.
fail_region.why_it_changed_again_in_v11: Three measured reasons. (i) TINT COLLISION: rulegrey!12 over white renders at grey 243 and panelbg at 244/242/237, within one level of each other, so the tint that means 'a measured region of outcome space' in panel (c) was the tint that means 'a schematic subspace' in panel (b) 3cm above it. rulegrey!8 renders at 246. Both are above the ink budget's 230 threshold, so neither costs anything against the ceiling. (ii) SIZE: at v10's span the region was 12.50 x 3.08cm = 21.6% of the content box, the largest object on the page, while the seven dots occupied a 2.5mm band. The RANGE is protected and untouched; the SPAN is a free choice and came 3.85 -> 3.00, so the region is 12.50 x 2.40cm = 16.8%. (iii) NAME: v10 emptied the region of text, which was right, and then left the largest mark on the page as the one mark a reader could not name -- and with it the third clause of this figure's acceptance test unanswerable from the drawing. The name is set OUTSIDE the region, so the emptiness is preserved.

schematic_marks_no_scale.v11_correction: THE PASS-6 LEGIBILITY REPAIR RECORDED HERE NEVER WORKED AND THIS ENTRY CERTIFIED IT FALSELY. At 2.8mm arms only the vertical arm was readable, exactly as at 2.0mm. Length was never the fault: three of the twelve displacement stems leave the vertex within 10 degrees of horizontal -- (-1.57,-0.085) at 3.1, (1.12,0.119) at 6.1, (1.40,-0.238) at -9.7 -- so the horizontal arm is buried in a near-collinear bundle at EVERY radius. v11 lays a 0.20cm disc of the band's own tint (white, then accent at fill opacity 0.12, byte-identical to the band, so the disc has no visible edge) over the stems and draws the cross in it, arms 0.34cm. schematic_marks_no_scale.colour_note_v11: the cross stays rulegrey, which is the corpus's register for a schematic unscaled mark. A refuter asked for ink on the ground that this file's own colour code reserves rulegrey for furniture; overruled, because the mark vocabulary assigns rulegrey to schematic marks explicitly and ink here would put a schematic glyph in the register of thresholds, axes and titles. The separation is made with white, not with colour.
